366750.title: Mandel's extension conjecture for oriented matroids
366750.literal_statement:
An **oriented matroid** is a combinatorial abstraction of a vector or hyperplane configuration, and an **extension** $\mathcal{O}\cup g$ adds a new ground-set element $g$; the extension is **in general position** when $g$ is not a coloop and satisfies the usual general-position condition. For elements $f$ of $\mathcal{O}$ that are neither loops nor coloops, $(\mathcal{O}\cup g,g,f)$ denotes the corresponding oriented matroid program.

**Mandel's conjecture.** Every oriented matroid $\mathcal{O}$ has an extension $g$ in general position (not a coloop) such that $(\mathcal{O}\cup g,g,f)$ is a Euclidean oriented matroid program for all elements $f$ of $\mathcal{O}$ that are not loops or coloops.

This conjecture is the source of the paper's definition of Mandel oriented matroids. The supplied text gives no resolution status or general theorem establishing the claim.

367232.title: Local-to-global conjugacy conjecture for Markov groups
367232.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the rooted ternary tree of height $n$, and let $M$ be the group arising from Sections 3 and 4. For subgroups $H,G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_n)$, say that $H$ is **locally conjugated** into $G$ if, for every $h\in H$, there exists $k$ in the kernel of the restriction map

$$
\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_n)\to\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_{n-1})
$$

such that $h^k\in G$. Say that $H$ is globally conjugated into $G$ if there exists one such $k$ with $H^k\subseteq G$.

**Local-to-global conjugacy conjecture.** If $H\leq\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_n)$ is locally conjugated into $M$, then $H$ is globally conjugated into $M$.

This is a group-theoretic conjecture intended to reduce questions about the Markov model to conjugacy inside automorphism groups of rooted trees. The source recalls it in the setting of the paper and does not state that it has been resolved.

367274.title: The dense analogue characterization conjecture for merge-width and flip-width
367274.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a graph class. Following the paper, say that $\mathcal C$ is in the **dense analogue of bounded expansion** if, for every weakly sparse graph class $\mathcal D$ such that $\mathcal C$ transduces $\mathcal D$, the class $\mathcal D$ has bounded expansion. **Dense analogue characterization conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(i)} & \mathcal C\text{ has bounded merge-width},\\
\text{(ii)} & \mathcal C\text{ has bounded flip-width},\\
\text{(iii)} & \mathcal C\text{ is in the dense analogue of bounded expansion}.
\end{array}
$$

The conjecture would provide an obstruction-based characterization of bounded merge-width and bounded flip-width. It is known in the paper for graph classes excluding a biclique as a subgraph and for classes of ordered graphs, while the general equivalence remains open.

367942.title: Intersection bounds for affine half-intervals over finite fields
367942.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be a finite field, and for $t\neq 0$ define

$$
S_n(s,t)=\{s+it\mid i\in[1,(n+1)/2]\}.
$$

For two such sets, multiplication by $t_1^{-1}$ and translation by $-s_1$ reduce their intersection to $S_n(0,1)\cap S_n(s_2-s_1,t_1^{-1}t_2)$.

**Intersection-bound conjecture.** If $t_1^{-1}t_2\notin\{1,n-1\}$, then

$$
|S_n(s_1,t_1)\cap S_n(s_2,t_2)|\leq\left\lceil\frac{n}{3}\right\rceil
$$

for all $s_1,s_2$. Moreover, if $t_1^{-1}t_2\notin\langle\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,\dots,\pm k\}\rangle$, then

$$
|S_n(s_1,t_1)\cap S_n(s_2,t_2)|\leq\left\lceil\frac{(k+1)n}{2(2k+1)}\right\rceil
$$

for all $s_1,s_2$.

These bounds are intended to control overlaps among the edge sets used in two-star-tree codes and could yield constructions less dependent on the parameter $m$. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution status, so the claim remains open.

368016.title: The freeness conjecture for GPTW-generated Lie subalgebras
368016.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a simplicial complex on $[m]$, let $\mathbf{k}$ be a commutative ring with unit, and define

$$
L_\mathcal{K}:=\operatorname{FL}_\mathbf{k}(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_m)/([\mu_i,\mu_j]=0,\ \forall\{i,j\}\in\mathcal{K}).
$$

Let $N_\mathcal{K}:=\langle\text{\it GPTW\/}\rangle_{\operatorname{Lie}}\subset L_\mathcal{K}$ be the Lie subalgebra generated by the Grbić–Panov–Theriault–Wu generators, and let $(N_\mathcal{K})_\alpha$ denote its multidegree-$\alpha$ component. **The freeness conjecture.** The module $N_\mathcal{K}$ is free over $\mathbf{k}$, with

$$
(N_\mathcal{K})_\alpha\simeq\mathbf{k}^{\oplus n_\alpha(\mathcal{K})}
$$

for every $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^m$; moreover, an analogue of the stated freeness and chordality theorem holds. 368064.title: Grassmannian and bigrassmannian signed permutation avoidance conjecture
368064.literal_statement:
Let $S_n^B$ denote the group of signed permutations of size $n$. A signed permutation is **Grassmannian** if it has a unique descent, and **bigrassmannian** if both it and its inverse have a unique descent. For a signed pattern $p$, say that a signed permutation **globally avoids** $p$ when no subsequence, with arbitrary signs, has underlying pattern $p$. Define

$$
P:=\{4321,32154,42153,43152,52143,53142,214365,315264,314265,415263\}.
$$

**Grassmannian and bigrassmannian avoidance conjecture.** A signed permutation is Grassmannian if and only if it globally avoids every pattern in $P$, and it is bigrassmannian if and only if it globally avoids every pattern in

$$
P\cup\{p^{-1}:p\in P\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes finite global-pattern characterizations for two classes whose classical type-A characterizations do not directly persist for signed permutations. The statement is presented as a conjectural analogue of the known type-A pattern-avoidance results.

368228.title: Zabrocki's nonnegativity conjecture for set-partition sums
368228.literal_statement:
For a positive integer $m$, let $[m]=\{1,\dots,m\}$, and let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be set partitions of $[m]$, with $\tau\ge\sigma$ meaning that every block of $\sigma$ is contained in some block of $\tau$. Write $\ell(\sigma)$ for the number of blocks of $\sigma$, let $(\lambda(\tau)-1)!$ denote the product of the factorials of one less than the number of elements in each block of $\tau$, and let $(\lambda(\sigma,\tau)-1)!$ denote the product of the factorials of one less than the number of blocks of $\sigma$ contained in each block of $\tau$. **Zabrocki's conjecture.** For every set partition $\sigma$ of $[m]$, the numbers

$$
\sum_{\tau\ge\sigma}(-1)^{\ell(\sigma)-\ell(\tau)} \frac{(\ell(\tau)-1)!(\lambda(\sigma,\tau)-1)!}{(\lambda(\tau)-1)!}
$$

are nonnegative. This conjecture concerns the sign pattern in the expansion of the $\mathbf{x}$-basis in the $\mathbf{e}$-basis for symmetric functions in noncommuting variables. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

368386.title: Mohan–Pandey conjecture on near-minimal restricted h-fold sumsets
368386.literal_statement:
Let $k$ be a large positive integer and let $h$ be a positive integer with

$$
2\leq h\leq k-2.
$$

Let $A$ be a finite set of $k$ nonnegative integers with $\min(A)=0$ and $d(A)=1$, where $d(A)$ is the greatest common divisor of all differences between elements of $A$. Write $h^{\wedge}A$ for the restricted $h$-fold sumset, consisting of sums of $h$ distinct elements of $A$.

**Mohan–Pandey conjecture.** The following implications hold:

(a) If $\left|h^{\wedge}A\right|=hk-h^2+2$, then $A\subset[0,k]$.

(b) If $\left|h^{\wedge}A\right|=hk-h^2+3$, then $A\subset[0,k+1]$.

(c) If $\left|h^{\wedge}A\right|=hk-h^2+4$, then $A\subset[0,k+2]$.

The conjecture extends the cited classifications of restricted double, triple, and quadruple sumsets to arbitrary positive $h$ in the stated range. The source describes $k$ only as large and gives no resolution.

368502.title: Falgas–Ravry's flat-interval conjecture
368502.literal_statement:
Let $\mathrm{T}[(r);a]$ be the generalized Turán pattern with parameter $r$ and ambient edge multiplicity $a$, and let $\Sigma_s(\mathrm{T}[(r);a])$ denote its associated threshold. **Falgas–Ravry's flat-interval conjecture.** For every $r,a\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ and every $s\geq 2r+1$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_\Pi\bigl(s,\Sigma_s(\mathrm{T}[(r);a])\bigr)=\cdots=\operatorname{ex}_\Pi\bigl(s,\Sigma_s(\mathrm{T}[(r);a])+\lfloor (s-1)/r\rfloor-1\bigr).
$$

In particular, for all $0\leq t\leq\lfloor (s-1)/r\rfloor-1$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_\Pi\bigl(s,\Sigma_s(\mathrm{T}[(r);a])+t\bigr)=a\left(\frac{a+1}{a}\right)^{(r-1)/r}.
$$

The conjecture predicts flat intervals of the multiplicative extremal function. The cited source presents it as an open conjecture; the surrounding paper gives supporting intuition but does not resolve it.
368502.finding: The proposed flat intervals concern the limiting multiplicative extremal function; a finite weighted graph beating one local value does not certify the claimed asymptotic endpoint.
368502.attempt_and_gap: Blow-ups of balanced Turan patterns give the asserted lower bound only. Need a matching all-graph upper bound throughout the interval, or an admissible blow-up beating it. No such construction found by ordinary reasoning.

368524.title: Gaetz–Gao's strong hull conjecture for Coxeter groups
368524.literal_statement:
Let $W$ be a Coxeter group, and let $\mathrm{Cay}(W)$ denote its undirected right Cayley graph associated with its generating set. For vertices $u,v,w\in V(\mathrm{Cay}(W))$, write $\mathrm{Conv}(u,v,w)$ for their convex hull, where convex hulls are taken with respect to graph distance. A graph has the strong hull property when

$$
|\mathrm{Conv}(u,v)|\cdot|\mathrm{Conv}(v,w)|\geq|\mathrm{Conv}(u,v,w)|
$$

for every three vertices $u,v,w$.

**Gaetz–Gao's strong hull conjecture.** Every Coxeter group $W$ has the property that its Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(W)$ satisfies the strong hull property.

Gaetz and Gao proposed this as a conjecture about convexity in Cayley graphs of Coxeter groups. The paper containing the statement proves it for all affine irreducible Coxeter groups of rank $3$; the general case remains open based on the supplied source.

369661.title: Local avoidance conjecture for polynomial images of integers and primes
369661.literal_statement:
Let $h\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a nonzero polynomial, and let $X=h(\mathbb{Z})$ or $X=h(\mathcal{P})$, where $\mathcal{P}$ denotes the set of primes. For each $m\in\mathbb{N}$, let $X_m$ be the set of congruence classes modulo $m$ that intersect $X$, and define

$$
d_X(m)=\max\{|A|: A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z},\ (A-A)\cap X_m=\emptyset\}.
$$

Here $\mu(X)$ denotes the maximal density of an $X$-set, namely a set whose pairwise differences avoid $X$. **Local avoidance conjecture.** For every such $h$ and $X$, we have

$$
\mu(X)=\sup_{m\in\mathbb{N}}\frac{d_X(m)}{m}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that for polynomial images of the integers and primes, the maximal global density of a set avoiding $X$-differences is determined by the strongest finite-modulus local avoidance obstruction. It extends the principle that local obstructions are the only obstructions in intersectivity questions; the supplied context does not state whether it is known or open.
369661.finding: Conjecture 2.3: periodic unions of congruence classes give the lower bound. The source identifies the upper bound as the content.
369661.attempt_and_gap: Subadditivity yields a global density limit but does not force optimal avoidance sets to be periodic for polynomial infinite forbidden sets. Intersective special cases and finite truncations do not solve all nonintersective polynomial images.

369775.title: Polynomial graph-partition conjecture for bounded-VC$_2$ hypergraphs
369775.literal_statement:

X\times Y=E_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup E_M,\quad X\times Z=F_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup F_M,\quad Y\times Z=G_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup G_M,

$$

370105.title: Optimal covering conjecture for small-doubling sumsets
370105.literal_statement:
Let $A$ be a set of size $s$ with doubling constant bounded by $K$, meaning $|A+A|\leq K|A|$. For each $ell$ let $\mathcal{F}_\ell$ be a collection of sets, and let $\tilde{O}$ and $\tilde{\Omega}$ suppress polylogarithmic factors in the relevant parameter. **Optimal covering conjecture.** There exist collections of sets $\mathcal{F}_\ell$ such that

$$
\log |\mathcal{F}_\ell|=\tilde{O}(2^\ell),
$$

and

$$
\min_{F\in\mathcal{F}_\ell}|F|=\tilde{\Omega}(2^\ell s),
$$

such that for every $A$ with $|A|=s$ and $|A+A|\leq K|A|$, there exists $\ell\leq\log_2 K$ and $F\in\mathcal{F}_\ell$ satisfying $A+A\supseteq F$. An optimal dependence on the doubling parameter would provide sharp obstructions for the independence number of sparse random Cayley graphs, up to logarithmic factors. 370593.title: Strong Schur log-concavity conjecture for diagonals of the quantum Pascal triangle

$$

370747.title: Lovett–Singer–Sudan conjecture on cross-intersecting set systems
370747.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}$ and $\mathcal{T}=\{T_1,\ldots,T_n\}$ be families in $2^{[d]}$, and suppose that $(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{T})$ is **$\{a,b\}$-cross-intersecting**, meaning that $|S\cap T|\in\{a,b\}$ for every $S\in\mathcal{S}$ and $T\in\mathcal{T}$, where $a,b\in\{0,\ldots,d\}$. **Lovett–Singer–Sudan conjecture.** There exist subfamilies $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{T}$ such that $(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$ is either $\{a\}$- or $\{b\}$-cross-intersecting, and

$$
|\mathcal{A}|,|\mathcal{B}|\geq 2^{-\operatorname{polylog}(d)}\cdot|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{T}|.
$$

This conjecture was independently proposed by Lovett and by Singer–Sudan, and the source says it is implied by the log-rank conjecture. The paper proves an equivalence between the two conjectures, so its resolution remains open.
370747.finding: The literal record bounds each of |A| and |B| below by a factor times |S||T|. Source Conjecture 1.6 bounds their product. This is a material transcription error; its source-corrected question is equivalent to log-rank by Theorem 1.7.
370747.attempt_and_gap: With S={empty} and T=2^[d], all intersections0, the literal individual bound eventually demands |A|>1 since 2^d dominates 2^polylog(d). This refutes a typo, earns zero, and does not touch the intended log-rank-equivalent claim.

371249.title: Fomichev–Karev conjecture on graph invariants
371249.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbf{G}$ be the set of isomorphism classes of finite simple graphs. For $G\in\mathbf{G}$, let $\varphi(G)$ be the graph invariant defined by

$$
\varphi(G)=2^{-3|V(G)|}\sum_{E'\subset E(G)}(-2)^{|E'|}\chi_3(G|_{E'}),
$$

where $\chi_3(G)$ is the number of proper vertex colorings of $G$ with three colors. Let

$$
\psi(G)=\frac{1}{2^{2|V(G)|}}\sum_{U\subset V(G)}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{|V(G)|-|U|}2^{\operatorname{corank}(A(G|_U))},
$$

where $G|_U$ is the induced subgraph on $U$, $A(G|_U)$ is its adjacency matrix over the field with two elements, and $\operatorname{corank}$ denotes matrix corank. **Fomichev–Karev conjecture.** For every $G\in\mathbf{G}$,

$$
\varphi(G)=\psi(G).
$$

Fomichev and Karev introduced these invariants in connection with graph Chmutov–Varchenko relations and the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-weight system. The conjecture is proved in the paper, so it is no longer open.
371249.finding: Yan-Deng-Jin arXiv2510.27279 Section2 proves the exact identity. Reindex kernel vectors by support, sum over intermediate subsets, use parity of boundary degrees, and obtain precisely Lemma2.1 Eulerian-subgraph formula for phi.
371249.attempt_and_gap: Every finite simple graph is covered; formalizing this existing proof has no new credit. Complete Section2 including Claim2.2 bijection and final parity calculation read.

371318.title: The characterization of Z-stable graph algebras by regularity and graph conditions
371318.literal_statement:
Let $E$ be a row-finite graph, and let $C^*(E)$ be its graph $C^*$-algebra. An elementary subquotient is a subquotient isomorphic to a compact-operator algebra; purity is the regularity property used in the paper. Condition (K) and distinct detours are graph-theoretic properties.

**Graph-algebra characterization conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

$$
C^*(E) \text{ is } \text{-stable},
$$

$$
C^*(E) \text{ has no elementary subquotients},
$$

$$
C^*(E) \text{ is pure},
$$

$$
E \text{ has Condition (K) and distinct detours}.
$$

The paper proves the corresponding equivalence for the graph-algebra results developed before the conjecture, including the relationship between no elementary subquotients, purity, Condition (K), and distinct detours. The full characterization for all row-finite graphs is proposed as an open problem.
371318.finding: Latest source proves finite/finitely-many-ideal cases and purity links but retains a general Z-stability conjecture. The literal rendering also drops the Z symbol.
371318.attempt_and_gap: Finite graph examples cannot settle all row-finite graphs. Purity-to-Z-stability requires a nontrivial operator-algebra theorem in the general ideal setting. No concrete full proof route.

361339.title: The strong approximation conjecture for the Markoff graph
361339.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be the set of Markoff triples over $\mathbb{Z}$, let $\mathcal{M}_p$ be the set of their reductions modulo a prime $p$, and let $\mathcal{G}^\times_p$ be the Markoff graph modulo $p$. The canonical projection identifies triples congruent modulo $p$. **Strong approximation conjecture.** For every prime $p$, the Markoff graph $\mathcal{G}^\times_p$ is connected and is equivalent to $\mathcal{G}^\times$ with triples congruent modulo $p$ identified; equivalently, the canonical projection $\mathcal{M}\to\mathcal{M}_p$ is onto. This conjecture asserts that every solution to the Markoff equation modulo a prime lifts to a Markoff triple over $\mathbb{Z}$. Strong approximation is known for all but finitely many primes, but remains open in general; it is a first step toward the expander-family conjecture for these graphs.
361339.finding: Source Conjectures1-2 and Lemma2 equate prime-modulus connectedness and lifting. Computation below a million and cofinite results leave finitely many unidentified cases, not a universal certificate.
361339.attempt_and_gap: No prime enumeration or Markoff numerical search. A finite algorithm at each input plus an unexplicit exceptional bound cannot establish all-prime connectedness.

361439.title: Generic non-optimality of constant potentials on non-path metric trees
361439.literal_statement:
Fix an underlying discrete tree graph that is not a path graph. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be its edge set, let the positive edge-length vector lie in $\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{E}|}_{+}$, and let $M>0$. For the corresponding metric tree $T$, let $C_{T,M}$ denote the class of convex potentials under consideration, and let the spectral gap be the difference between the first two eigenvalues.

**Generic non-optimality conjecture.** The set of edge-length vectors and values $M>0$ for which the constant potential minimizes the spectral gap in $C_{T,M}$ is of the first Baire category in

$$
\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{E}|}_{+}\times\mathbb{R}_{+}.
$$

The claim concerns the generic behavior of convex-potential gap minimization on metric trees and asserts that constant potentials are exceptional for every underlying tree that is not a path graph. The source presents it as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
361439.finding: Source Conjecture5.1 is a first-Baire-category assertion over all lengths and M, not a statement about one nonconstant minimizing example.
361439.attempt_and_gap: Feynman-Hellmann negativity at an individual leaf gives local nonminimality and openness, not meagreness of all minimizers. Need perturbation density on each tree topology with eigenvalue multiplicities controlled. Parked without numerical experiments.
